div.p: Background Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most prevalent and challengingto-diagnose brain tumor, is a highly lethal and largely untreatable form of brain cancer. Circular RNAs (CircRNAs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) may serve as biomarkers for GBM diagnosis and treatment. Circ_100290 and miR-205-5p play a key role in gene regulation, tumor progression, and cellular communication, making them valuable biomarkers for GBM, but their precise role in GBM remains unclear and requires further investigation.

Methods Bioinformatics analyses were conducted to explore interactions between miR-205-5p and circ_100290, their functional roles, and associated pathways. Additionally, we assessed the differences of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 between tumor and normal samples by analyzing the quantitative real-time PCR.

div.head: Results
div.p: Bioinformatics analysis revealed a network association of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 to key proteins (PTEN, SMAD4, CDK19, ELAVL1, HNRNPK, DDX5, AGO2, and EIF4A3) and pathways, including Wnt signaling, highlighting their roles in splicing and gene expression regulation and the regulation of tumor development and metastasis. QRT-PCR analysis revealed a significant downregulation of miR-205-5p and an upregulation of circ_100290 compared to normal tissues. Notably, the downregulation of miR-205-5p was associated with increased tumor volume and lobar tumor localization, whereas the upregulation ofcirc_100290 correlated with IDH1 gene mutations in GBM patients.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: Our study highlights miR-205-5p downregulation and circ_100290 upregulation in GBM patients which underscore their diagnostic potential and cooperative role in GBM progression, offering novel insights for therapeutic targeting.

div.head: Background
div.p: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is an aggressive and highly malignant brain tumor, representing one of the most prevalent and complex forms of brain cancer. It constitutes nearly 50% of all brain tumors, presenting considerable challenges in both diagnosis and treatment [1]. e tumor is characterized by its rapid and aggressive growth, as well as its invasive growth pattern and extensive angiogenesis. Historically, the standard treatment for glioblastoma has involved surgery combined with radiation and chemotherapy. However, patients with this particular brain tumor often face a grim prognosis. Gliomas, including glioblastoma, exhibit a high resistance to conventional therapies, resulting in low survival rates [2]. In the development of glioma, epigenetic factors play vital roles and serve as both potent predictors and determinants of resistance to radiation and chemotherapy [3]. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs) are three forms of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) that have been shown to have an association with the development of neoplastic diseases. Circular RNAs were previously included in all coding RNAs, but they are now considered their distinct subfamily. Circular RNAs are distinctive due to their "exon skipping" or "direct back-splicing" mechanisms, which markedly differentiate them from other RNAs in terms of their non-linear nature. Instead of possessing 5′ caps and 3′ tails, these molecules exhibit a continuous closed-loop structure [4]. e expression of genes in mammals is regulated in part by these chemicals [5][6][7]. On the contrary, they have numerous roles, encompassing acting as a miRNA reservoir, engaging with RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), transcription and regulating splicing, translation and generating pseudogenes, and transmission and correspondence. CircRNAs can also regulate gene expression by impacting transcription mechanisms [8]. Circular RNAs have been shown to affect cell proliferation, differentiation, and migration in various cancer types, including hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and GBM. e PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway has a mediating role in these outcomes [2]. Additionally, the Wnt signaling pathway, known for its critical role in regulating cell proliferation, differentiation, and stemness, is frequently dysregulated in various cancers, including GBM [9]. Aberrant activation of this pathway is closely linked to tumor progression and resistance to therapy. Emerging evidence also suggests potential interactions between Wnt signaling and non-coding RNAs, such as miRNAs and circRNAs, highlighting their combined influence on cancer biology [9,10]. MicroRNAs, a class of untranslated RNAs, serve as mediators and intergene connectors within non-coding RNAs. Specific miRNAs show promise as predictive clinical biomarkers for predicting prognosis, diagnosing tumors, and assessing treatment response; these molecules significantly impact cancer initiation and progression. MicroRNAs can act in one of two opposing ways: As oncogenes or as tumor suppressors. Examining the distinct mRNA expression profile associated with GBM effectively highlight the significance of specific miRNAs in GBM development. is profile is a crucial factor in the diagnosis and prognosis of cancers in this family (2). MiRNAs have a significant role in regulating gene expression during the development and differentiation of immune cells, and in the nervous system. Changes in the levels of expression of various miRNAs, along with alterations in protein expression, can disrupt immune functions and cause damage to tissues in the nervous system [11,12]. Many cancers, including GBM, have been linked to dysregulation of microRNA expression as a component in their development and progression. One such example is the downregulation of miR-4731, which has been linked to the progression of GBM. For this reason, it is crucial to investigate the central role of miRNAs in the onset of tumor formation and the subsequent dissemination of cancer cells. Despite the usefulness of biomarkers in the diagnosis of certain types of solid tumors, it is clear that additional diagnostic procedures are necessary [3]. It is suspected that miR-205-5p affects several cells signaling pathways linked to migration, proliferation, and death and that this miRNA is involved in angiogenesis related to the VEGFA gene. In addition, miR-205-5p may have anti-angiogenic characteristics, according to prior studies. Research has demonstrated that miR-205-5p suppresses tumor cell migration and proliferation in glioblastoma through either target gene downregulation or direct growth inhibition [13]. Beyond glioblastoma, this miRNA serves as a valuable prognostic marker in pancreatic, prostate, and bladder malignancies [14,15]. e regulatory landscape of cancer progression also involves circular RNAs, which exert their effects by competitively binding to miRNAs through the ceRNA mechanism [16]. is interaction allows circRNAs to influence key oncogenic pathways, with growing recognition of their pathological significance in glioma development [17]. Particularly relevant is circRNA_100290, which drives tumorigenesis in various cancers (colorectal, gastric, laryngeal) via activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascade [18]. Although its oncogenic functions are well-characterized in oral and myeloid malignancies [16], its role in glioblastoma pathogenesis remains unexplored. Emerging data indicate a potential regulatory relationship between hsa_circRNA_100290 and miR-205-5p in GBM, possibly mediated through competitive binding to common targets, thereby influencing critical cancer hallmarks including proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis. Despite these insights, the functional interplay between miR-205-5p and hsa_cir-cRNA_100290 in GBMremains largely unexplored.

In the present study, the expression levels of miR-205-5p and circRNA_100290 in FFPE GBM tumor and normal tissues were assessed using RT-qPCR. Additionally, the molecular interactions and correlations of miR-205-5p and circRNA_100290 with key proteins and signaling pathways were investigated through comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. Subsequently, the associations between the expression levels of these molecules and clinicopathological features were analyzed. ese findings suggest that miR-205-5p and circRNA_100290 may play significant roles in GBM pathogenesis and could serve as potential therapeutic targets.

div.head: Acquisition of GBM gene expression data from GEO databases
div.p: To examine the expression profiles of miR-205-5p and circ_100290, we retrieved the GSE90603 and GSE146463 datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. e expression levels of these non-coding RNAs in GBM versus normal samples were analyzed using GEO2R (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/geo2r/).

div.head: Prediction of miR-205-5p target genes
div.p: To predict potential target genes of miR-205-5p, we utilized the microRNA Data Integration Portal (miRDIP) (https://ophid.utoronto.ca/mirDIP/) [19], which integrates p r e d i c t i o n s from twelve independent microRNA prediction datasets across six databases.

div.head: Prediction of hsa_circ_100290 RNA-binding protein
div.p: Potential RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) interacting with hsa_circ_100290 were predicted using Circular RNA Interactome (CircInteractome) ( h t t p s : / / c i r c i n t e r a c t o m e . n i a . n i h . g o v / ) [20]. is analysis was based on crosslinking immunoprecipitation (CLIP) data, identifying proteins that interact with RNA molecules.

div.head: PPI network and pathway enrichment analysis
div.p: To explore molecular interactions, we constructed a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) networks using the STRING database (version 10.5) (http://string-db.org/), applying a high-confidence interaction threshold (>0.9). Additionally, a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network, including miR-205-5p, circ_100290, and associated mRNAs, was visualized using Cytoscape (version 3.6.1) (http://www.cytoscape.org/) [21]. Key hub genes within the network were identified using the cytoHubba plugin, based on degree centrality. To further understand the biological functions of these genes, Gene Ontology (GO) biological process and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses were performed using Enrichr (https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/), and results were visualized using Enrichr-KG [22].

div.head: Patients and sample collection
div.p: In this study, a total of 20 formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue samples, including tumor and normal tissues, were collected. Samples were obtained from patients who underwent surgical resection at Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, during 2020 to 2022. None of the patients had previously undergone chemotherapy or radiotherapy. GBM cases were classified according to the 2007 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (CNS) by experienced clinical pathologists. Clinicopathological parameters, including gender, age distribution, anatomic tumor localization, tumor hemisphere, tumor size, and isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) status, were extracted from medical records and analyzed.
e study was conducted with ethical approval (Code: IR.IAU.TNB.REC.1401.046) obtained from the Research Ethics Committee of the Islamic Azad University, North Tehran Branch.

div.head: RNA extraction and purification
div.p: RNA extraction was performed using the RNrich FFPE Tissue Paraffin Extraction Kit (AZMA ELIXIR, Iran, #1103) according to the manufacturer's protocol. Briefly, FFPE tissue sections underwent deparaffinization with xylene and were rehydrated using a graded ethanol series. Proteinase K was then used to digest the tissues, enabling protein removal and RNA release. RNA extraction was carried out using the kit's proprietary buffer system, followed by purification through sequential washing and elution steps. RNA quality and quantity were assessed using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer ( ermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). Purity was determined by measuring the absorbance ratios at 260/280 nm and 260/230 nm, with values of ~ 2.0 and ~ 2.2, respectively, indicating high-purity RNA.

div.head: cDNA synthesis and qRT-PCR analysis
div.p: cDNA synthesis for microRNA was performed using the TaqMan™ Advanced miRNA cDNA Synthesis Kit ( ermo Scientific, USA, #A28007), while cDNA synthesis for circRNA was carried out using the AmpliSens RT Reagents Kit (AmpliSens, Russia, Cat. #K3-4-50-CE), following the respective protocols. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) was conducted using the Step One Real-Time PCR System (QIAGEN, Germany) with SYBR Premix Ex Taq II (Takara, Japan). U6 and GAPDH were used as endogenous controls for miR-205-5p and circ_100290, respectively. U6 and GAPDH were selected as endogenous controls for miR-205-5p and circ_100290, respectively, based on their common use in qPCR studies. While formal stability validation using algorithms like geNorm was not performed, we observed consistent Ct values across samples (SD < 1.5 cycles for both genes), suggesting acceptable stability in our experimental conditions. e potential impact of RNA degradation in FFPE samples on reference gene stability has been considered in the study limitations. e thermocycling conditions included an initial denaturation at 95 °C for 1 min, followed by 40 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s, 55 °C for 30 s, and 70 °C for 30 s. Relative gene expression levels were calculated using the 2 -ΔΔCt method, with normalization to the endogenous controls. Primer sequences for miR-205-5p and circ_100290 were designed using Primer-BLAST [23] and CircInteractome software [24], with detailed primer information provided in Table 1.

div.head: Examining association of expression and clinicopathological features
div.p: Pearson's correlation analysis was performed to explore the association between miR-205-5p and circ_100290 expression patterns and the clinicopathological variables, including gender, age distribution, anatomic tumor localization, location hemisphere, tumor size, and IDH1 status.

div.head: Statistical analysis
div.p: We determined the expression levels of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 based on their threshold cycle (CT) values.

e normality and log-normality of qPCR data were assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test prior to applying parametric tests. Consequently, the Mann-Whitney U test was applied to evaluate differences in miR-205-5p and circ_100290 expression levels between GBM and normal samples. GraphPad Prism version 8.4.3 (GraphPad Software, La Jolla, CA, USA) was used to analyze the qPCR results and generate graphical representations. For multiple comparisons, P-values were adjusted using the Holm-Bonferroni correction. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 18.0 (SPSS Inc., Chicago, USA), and all data were presented as mean values ± standard deviation (SD). A P-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

div.head: Expression levels of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 based on GEO datasets
div.p: To investigate the potential roles of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 in glioblastoma (GBM), we first analyzed their expression levels using public microarray datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). e GSE90603 dataset was selected for its comprehensive miRNA expression data in GBM and matched normal tissues, with GEO2R used to normalize data and minimize batch effects. Our analysis revealed that miR-205-5p showed a slightly higher median expression in GBM samples compared to normal samples (P = 0.241, FC = 0.1869879), but this difference was not statistically significant (Fig. 1a).

In contrast, circ_100290 exhibited significantly higher expression in GBM samples compared to normal samples (P = 0.007, FC = 0.6151391, GSE146463) (Fig. 1b). ese findings suggest that while miR-205-5p expression may vary subtly in GBM, circ_100290 is consistently upregulated, prompting us to explore their molecular interactions in GBM.

Although the in-silico analysis revealed that changes in the expression of miR-205-5p were not statistically significant, investigating its target genes and the network it forms with circ_100290 may yield valuable insights into its functional role in glioblastoma.

div.head: How do miR-205-5p and circ_100290 interact in GBM molecular networks?
div.p: e molecular network linking the target genes regulated by miR-205-5p and the RBPs associated with circ_100290 (Fig. 2) was established within the PPI network. e interactions with the highest confidence (> 0.900) were defined as default. As depicted in Fig. 3, both miR-205-5p and circ_100290 share common interactions with pivotal proteins, Fig. 1 Expression levels of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 in GEO datasets. a, miR-205-5p shows a slightly higher median expression in GBM samples compared to normal samples, but the difference is not statistically significant (P = 0.241, FC = 0.1869879, GSE90603). b, circ_100290 is significantly upregulated in GBM samples compared to normal samples (P = 0.007, FC = 0.6151391, GSE146463). (*P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001, ns: not significant)

including PTEN, SMAD4, CDK19, ELAVL1, HNRNPK, DDX5, AGO2, and EIF4A3. Nodes' sizes are determined by their statistical importance within the network and their inclusion in the hub-genes list. Finally, an investigation was conducted using enrichment analysis to explore shared molecular pathways between miR-205-5p and circ_100290.

e results in (Fig. 4a, b) demonstrated the clustering of genes within the ceRNA network and allowed for the determination of their associations with various KEGG pathways and biological processes. Collectively, these findings suggest that miR-205-5p, circ_100290, and their associated downstream gene network may play a significant role Fig. 2 RNA-binding protein (RBP) sites associated with circ_100290. The figure illustrates the predicted binding sites of RBPs interacting with circ_100290, retrieved from the Circular RNA Interactome database

in glioblastoma tumorigenesis. However, in line with the primary objective of this study, our key focus was to determine whether these two non-coding RNAs could serve as potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers in patient-derived samples. Accordingly, their expression levels were examined through experimental analysis (Fig. 4a, b).

div.head: GBM patients' characteristics for mRNA expression analysis
div.p: To validate our bioinformatics findings, we analyzed a cohort of 20 GBM patients whose formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples were used for expression studies. Regarding sex distribution, 11 (55.0%) were male, and 9 (45.0%) were female. Amongst the 12 patients, the median age was less than or equal to 57 years, constituting 60% of the total, and also, in the remaining eight patients, the median age surpassed 57 years, accounting for 40% of the total. Moreover, among the 11 cases, the median tumor size was less than or equal to 5 cm, representing 55% of the total. Conversely, in the remaining 9 cases, the median tumor size exceeded 5 cm, making up 45% of the total. In two patients (2 cases; 10.0%), the GBM tumor was located in the occipital lobe. Among the remaining patients, the tumor distribution was as follows: temporal lobe (8 cases; 40.0%), multilobe (4 cases; 20.0%), frontal lobe (6 cases; 30.0%). Regarding hemispheric Fig. 4 Enrichment analysis of miR-205-5p and circ_100290-associated pathways. a, Gene ontology (GO) biological processes highlighting their roles in splicing, gene expression regulation, and other cellular functions. b, KEGG pathways, including key signaling pathways such as Wnt signaling. Orange lines indicate gene co-expression within the ceRNA network location, the tumor was found in the right hemisphere (13 cases; 65.0%) and in the left hemisphere (7 cases; 35.0%). In terms of IDH1 status, wild-type and mutant were observed in (9 cases; 45.0%) and (11 cases; 55.0%), respectively. Detailed tumoral characteristics are described in Table 2. ese patient characteristics provide a foundation for analyzing the associations between miR-205-5p and circ_100290 expression and clinicopathological features in GBM.

div.head: Are miR-205-5p and circ_100290 differentially expressed in GBM tumor samples?
div.p: We conducted qRT-PCR analysis to investigate the expression levels of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 in two distinct sets of samples. Our results revealed a significant downregulation of miR-205-5p expression in GBM samples compared to the corresponding normal samples (P-value = 0.002) (Fig. 5a). Additionally, our findings demonstrated a noticeable upregulation of circ_100290 expression in GBM samples compared to normal samples (P-value = 0.026) (Fig. 5b). ese findings validate the GEO data for circ_100290 and highlight a distinct expression pattern for miR-205-5p in clinical samples, suggesting their potential as diagnostic biomarkers and prompting further investigation into their clinical implications.

div.head: Associations between miR-205-5p, circ_100290, and clinicopathological features
div.p: Pearson's chi-square analysis demonstrated a statistically significant correlation between miR-205-5p expression levels and both tumor size (P-value = 0.025) and tumor lobe location (P-value = 0.007) (Table 3). Furthermore, significant differences were observed in the median circ_100290 expression levels in relation to IDH1 status (P-value = 0.008) (Table 4). ese associations underscore the potential of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 as prognostic markers in GBM, linking their expression to aggressive tumor characteristics.

To further investigate these associations, we performed the Mann-Whitney test to compare groups. Notably, we observed an upregulation of miR-205-5p expression in Table2 Characteristics of the entire study population tumors located in the left lobe compared to the right lobe (P-value = 0.005) (Fig. 6a). Conversely, a downregulation of miR-205-5p expression was observed in tumors with a median size exceeding 5 cm compared to those with a size less than or equal to 5 cm (P-value = 0.031) (Fig. 6b). Additionally, regarding IDH1 status, circ_100290 expression was significantly upregulated in tumors with mutant IDH1 compared to those with the wild-type gene (P-value = 0.036) (Fig. 6c).

div.head: Discussion
div.p: GBM remains one of the most lethal brain cancers, responsible for nearly half of all primary brain tumors [25]. Its treatment is challenging due to high cellular heterogeneity and multiple genetic alterations affecting cell cycle regulation, growth, apoptosis, and invasion. Despite aggressive therapies, median survival remains limited to 12-15 months [26][27][28]. Identifying novel biomarkers is crucial for accurate diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and selecting effective therapeutic strategies [27,29]. Non-coding RNAs, including miRNAs and circRNAs, play crucial roles in gene regulation and cancer progression. CircRNAs act as competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs), sponging miRNAs and modulating tumorigenesis [1-3, 30, 31]. MiR-205-5p has been implicated in both oncogenic and tumor-suppressive functions, depending on the cellular context [32][33][34]. However, Table 4 The correlation between the expressions of circ_100290 and clinicopathological parameters its precise role in GBM remains unclear. is study investigates the differential expression of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 in GBM and their association with key clinicopathological parameters.
Our findings reveal a significant downregulation of miR-205-5p and upregulation of circ_100290 in GBM samples compared to normal tissues, consistent with previous research [28,35].

Notably, lower miR-205-5p levels correlated with larger tumor sizes, reinforcing its tumor-suppressive role [36]. Notably, we observed significantly elevated miR-205-5p expression in left-hemisphere gliomas compared to right-hemisphere tumors, indicating potential hemisphere-specific regulatory roles. However, the functional significance of miR-205-5p in glioma pathogenesis remains poorly understood, with limited evidence regarding its impact on critical oncogenic processes [37]. ese findings highlight the diagnostic and prognostic potential of miR-205-5p in GBM [32,[38][39][40].

e upregulation of circ_100290 in GBM, particularly in tumors harboring IDH1 mutations, suggests its involvement in IDH1-driven oncogenic processes. Genetic and epigenetic alterations affecting circRNA biogenesis may underlie these changes, as IDH1 and IDH2 mutations have been linked to altered epigenetic landscapes and circRNA expression [41].
e significant upregulation of circ_100290 in IDH1-mutant tumors warrants further validation in larger cohorts, such as TCGA or CGGA, to confirm its role as a potential biomarker in GBM.

Pathway enrichment analysis identified miR-205-5p and circ_100290 as key regulators of oncogenic pathways, including PTEN/PI3K/AKT, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and Wnt signaling [32,[42][43][44][45][46][47]. Reduced miR-205-5p expression may enhance tumor growth, invasion, and apoptosis resistance in GBM [14, 48-50, 50, 51]. Given the critical role of Wnt signaling in GBM pathogenesis, its dual function in maintaining normal tissue homeostasis while promoting oncogenesis presents both challenges and opportunities for targeted therapy [9,10,52] Our findings suggest that miR-205-5p and circ_100290 may indirectly modulate Wnt signaling, contributing to GBM pathogenesis. Beyond GBM, miR-205-5p downregulation has been observed in osteosarcoma, breast cancer, pancreatic cancer, and prostate cancer, where it affects tumor proliferation, apoptosis, and drug sensitivity, correlating with poor prognosis [15,[53][54][55][56]. Similarly, circ_100290 exhibits variable expression across different cancers. Its overexpression in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), colorectal cancer (CRC), and gastric cancer (GC) [50 ]. Elevated circ_100290 levels in LSCC and OSCC were linked to increased proliferation, invasion, and metastasis [57,58], while in GC, it was associated with EMT through miR-29b-3p interaction [59].

ese findings reinforce the potential oncogenic role of circ_100290 invarious cancers [50,59,60]. While miR-205-5p and circ_100290 did not show a strong direct correlation in GBM, network analysis revealed shared regulatory interactions. PPI network analysis identified key regulators, including PTEN, SMAD4, CDK19, ELAVL1, HNRNPK, DDX5, AGO2, and EIF4A3. MiR-205-5p is known to regulate essential cellular processes such as growth, apoptosis, and angiogenesis by targeting key oncogenes [32,61]. Additionally, EIF4A3, an RNA-binding protein with a strong affinity for circ_100290, has been implicated in stabilizing proteins and enhancing tumorigenesis across various cancers, including glioblastoma, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), pancreatic cancer, and ovarian cancer [59,62]. Interestingly, Wang et al. demonstrated that EIF4A3 may inhibit circ_100290 formation by binding to its adjacent regions, potentially under self-regulation [59]. Further analysis indicates that miR-205-5p may exert indirect regulation over EIF4A3, with both molecules potentially impacting the Wnt signaling pathway.

Notably, our GEO analysis did not reveal significant differential expression of miR-205-5p, which contrasts with studies reporting its downregulation in GBM and other cancers [48,51,61,63,64]. In contrast, circ_100290 upregulation in GBM supports its potential oncogenic role, highlighting its significance in tumor progression [50,59,60]. GBM is characterized by extensive molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity that influences genetic backgrounds, tumor behavior, and therapeutic responses.

is heterogeneity likely contributes to the observed variability in miR-205-5p and circ_100290 expression profiles across our study's GBM cohort. For instance, the non-significant upregulation of miR-205-5p in GEO dataset GSE90603 (P = 0.241) contrasted with its significant downregulation in our FFPE samples (P = 0.002), potentially reflecting differences in tumor subtypes, genetic backgrounds (e.g., IDH1 mutation status), or microenvironmental factors such as hypoxia or immune infiltration.

is discrepancy may reflect selection bias in the choice of GEO datasets, as not all eligible datasets exhibited concordant expression changes. Future studies will implement a predefined, systematic screening strategy to select datasets, minimizing such bias and enhancing the reliability of in-silico findings. Although miR-205-5p has been implicated in angiogenesis regulation via VEGFA in other cancers [53], our study did not measure VEGFA mRNA/protein levels. Variations in genetic backgrounds (e.g., IDH1 mutation status) and tumor microenvironmental factors likely contribute to these differences. While our network analysis aligns with the hypothesis of miR-205-5p's anti-angiogenic role, and bioinformatics data suggest regulation of Wnt/PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways by miR-205-5p and circ_100290, direct experimental validation of downstream effectors (e.g., β-catenin, phosphorylated Akt, or VEGFA) is needed to confirm these interactions. In vitro and in vivo experiments, such as gene knockdown or overexpression studies, are needed to validate the functional roles of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 in GBM pathogenesis. Future studies incorporating single-cell RNA sequencing or spatial transcriptomics could better elucidate how tumor heterogeneity influences the roles of these non-coding RNAs in GBM.

div.head: Limitations
div.p: Given the complex and multifactorial nature of glioblastoma (GBM), this study has several limitations. e sample size (n = 20) is relatively small, which may limit the statistical power and generalizability of our findings regarding the expression of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 and their associations with clinicopathological features. GBM is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy, with an incidence of approximately 3-4 per 100,000 individuals, making it challenging to obtain a large number of high-quality formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples suitable for qRT-PCR analysis. e limited availability of samples, coupled with logistical constraints such as restricted access to patients meeting inclusion criteria (e.g., no prior or radiotherapy) and technical difficulties in tissue preservation and RNA extraction, restricted our cohort size. Additionally, GBM's significant molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity, driven by diverse genetic backgrounds (e.g., IDH1 mutations) and tumor microenvironmental factors, likely influenced the variability in miR-205-5p and circ_100290 expression observed in our study, such as the discrepancy between GEO and FFPE results for miR-205-5p. e small sample size and use of FFPE tissues limited our ability to fully capture this heterogeneity. Another limitation is the lack of experimental validation for downstream proteins, such as β-catenin, phosphorylated Akt, and VEGFA, implicated in the Wnt and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways identified through bioinformatics analysis. Specifically, the expression of VEGFA mRNA and protein was not measured due to the technical challenges of protein analysis in FFPE samples, where protein degradation during fixation and paraffinization limits reliable quantification, and the study's primary focus on noncoding RNA expression via qRT-PCR. e absence of in vitro and in vivo experiments to confirm the functional roles of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 in these pathways, as well as their anti-angiogenic effects via VEGFA, further restricts mechanistic insights. Validation of circ_100290 upregulation in IDH1-mutant tumors using larger external cohorts, such as TCGA or CGGA, was not feasible due to resource constraints. Our findings require validation in larger, independent external cohorts, such as TCGA or CGGA, to confirm their diagnostic and prognostic potential. Confirmatory analysis in public datasets represents a critical next step to strengthen these observations. Future studies with larger and more diverse cohorts, potentially through collaborations with international cancer registries, and the use of fresh-frozen tissues or advanced techniques such as single-cell RNA sequencing or spatial transcriptomics, are planned to address these limitations, capture GBM heterogeneity, and enhance the robustness of our findings.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: In summary, our study demonstrates that miR-205-5p acts as a tumor suppressor in GBM, with significant correlations to tumor size and location, while circ_100290 expression is associated with IDH1 mutation status, suggesting its involvement in metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. Network analysis further highlights their shared associations with key regulatory proteins (e.g., PTEN, SMAD4, EIF4A3) and oncogenic pathways, including Wnt signaling. ese findings underscore the potential of miR-205-5p and circ_100290 as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in GBM. Further research is needed to fully elucidate their molecular mechanisms, which could lead to innovative therapeutic strategies and improved management of GBM.

div.p: There is no funding or support.

div.head: Data availability
div.p: The gene expression datasets analyzed in this study are publicly available in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/). The miRNA expression data were retrieved from the GSE90603 dataset .ncbi.nlm.n ih.gov/geo/ query/ac c.cgi? acc=GSE90603), and the circRNA expression data were obtained from the GSE146463 dataset (https://www .ncbi.nlm.n ih.gov/geo/ query/ac c.cgi? acc=GSE146463). Additional bioinformatics analyses were performed using publicly accessible databases, including miRDIP (https://ophid.utoronto.ca/mirDIP/) for miR-205-5p target prediction, CircInteractome (https://circinteractome.nia.nih.gov/) for RNA-binding protein prediction, STRING (http://string-db.org/) for protein-protein interaction network analysis, and Enrichr ( h t t p s : / / m a a y a n l a b . c l o u d / E n r i c h r / ) for Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis.

div.head: Declarations Ethics approval and consent to participate
div.p: All experiments involving human tissue samples were performed in accordance with the ethical standards of the Declaration of Helsinki and other relevant guidelines and regulations. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the Islamic Azad University, North Tehran Branch, under ethics code IR.IAU.TNB.REC.1401.046. Written informed consent was obtained from the legal guardians or next of kin of all participants for their participation in this study.
